requirement:
Plain text defines no attachments. The file root and each `line` item have
empty attachment lists, including lines that begin with comment delimiters
from another language.
rationale:
**Obligation.** `requirements.sdk.sources.plain-text.attachments` says three things:
- The plain-text file root has an empty attachment list.
- Each `line` item has an empty attachment list.
- This holds even for lines that begin with comment delimiters from another language.

**Test.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` carries a `{test}` reference to the requirement. Its `test.txt` case parses `"# just text\n"` through `OutlineContent::from_source`. That text is a line beginning with a foreign (Python, TOML or YAML) comment delimiter. The test then:
- collects the attachments of every item in `outline().items`, using `flat_map`;
- asserts that the collected list equals `vec![]`.

**Why the root and line items are both covered.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]` asserts that a plain-text outline has three items for two nonblank lines, "Root and two nonblank lines". The `flat_map` therefore includes the root and the line item. The assertion would fail if any of them received a `Comment` or `Annotation` attachment. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes]` shows that plain-text lines produce line items. So the empty result is not vacuous.

**Counterexample check.** Suppose an implementation classified `#` lines as comments in plain text. The assertion on the `test.txt` case would catch it. The same test checks other languages' syntax at the same time, which shows the classifiers are language-specific.

**Coverage limits.** Only the `#` delimiter is exercised. The requirement says "comment delimiters from another language" generically. The plain-text implementation, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/mod.rs#fn[plain_text]`, has no per-delimiter distinction, so other delimiters add no distinct input class. I found no gap.
